title: Remove protections against hypothetical file swaps (same_file and share-mode pinning) where they guard no real scenario
outcome: Remove protections against hypothetical file swaps (same_file and share-mode pinning) where they guard no real scenario
acceptance: The physical file and directory identity proofs (PhysicalId, file_identity, Directory::identity) in src/task_sync/setup/materialize (journal, completion, replacement, publication) and src/task_sync/setup/files.rs are removed; the restore same_file held-versus-named check, graph publication's held ancestor chain, SUBST volume-root check and reparse/real-directory walk, and both share_mode(1) uses (bin_support/source_identity.rs, task_sync/setup/files.rs) are removed; each site's keep/remove classification is recorded on the item (Inquisitor note 0d096353)

Kept and still working: resume after interruption from an admitted journal (including journals written before identities were dropped), no-replace publication, preservation of the set-aside before file, the real UNC full-path removal in backup restore, the rule that a graph snapshot never lands in Engram's project stores as a resolved-path comparison, is_same_file and same_directory comparisons of the user's two spellings, share_mode(7), and a plain same-filesystem refusal before a materialization attempt is created
The removed protections' tests and documentation are deleted with no replacement check, scanner or identity mechanism, and the surrounding real recovery behaviour tests pass
Reviewer findings whose only trigger is a hypothetical swap, rename, alias or concurrent writer are rejected, per rules-greg-no-hypothetical-protections-2026-11-21

completion.summary: Completed the simplification on landed Engram master and verified it on the named post-landing root. The fresh independent acceptance evaluation passed all four criteria; the focused Central restore test passed 36/36, and the evaluator verified the preserved recovery and publication behavior alongside removal of the hypothetical-swap protections.
